status: in progress; full throughput/memory parity remains unmet

build.source_attribution: Event-only source matches archived event-every-task-main.rs byte for byte after rejection/restoration of global-queue experiment. No formatting-only rebuild after the freeze.

implementation: For the default CLI WebTransport runtime, poll I/O/timers after every scheduled task instead of Tokio 1.53.3 default 61. Existing global-queue scheduling remains unchanged. Native WebSocket continues its separate Mio workers/current-thread management runtime. No transport/crypto/framing, message/resource limits, queue semantics or deadlines change.
tradeoffs: Reliable fanout improves in two matched blocks, while private-only throughput decreases about 3% and CPU cost rises at a fixed 100k offered load and in datagram echoes. This is an explicit workload tradeoff, not a mixed-private fairness fix or a general claim of lower overhead.
scope: Shared Linux host. No concurrent task-owned builds/tests/browser during ordinary timings. Fixed client executables. Each matched block alternates fresh processes three times per case/variant. Four pinned server workers 0-3, eight pinned client workers 8-15, four seconds, 1 KiB, 32 private pairs, 1024 room readers, fanout window four. Capacity uses eight pinned server and eight pinned client workers, 100k physical connections and four offered seconds. Logarithmic latency percentiles are upper bounds, RSS excludes kernel allocations. Absolute rates vary substantially between blocks; do not pool blocks or compare cherry-picked rates.

server.scope: Process-owned connected TCP sockets or bound UDP sockets, filtered by the requested ports. skmem fields are separate counters, not an additive total. Buffer limits are not allocations. Slab object estimate excludes slab overhead, protocol buffers, route/conntrack state and other kernel resources. TIME_WAIT port matches have no live fd and are reported separately. This is not complete kernel memory accounting.

kernel_tests.scope: Real queued UDP allocations cross-checked with ss and SO_RCVBUF; IPv4/IPv6 TCP endpoint ownership and queued-data checks; malformed/truncated binary messages fail instead of undercounting.

validation.vendor: 153 files against four pinned archives and three patches; dependency source unchanged

browser.scope: Actual delivered bundle in Chromium: all nine typed/control/private/broadcast/datagram/large-message/closure checks, including 5 MiB.

rejected_global_queue_trial.scope: Same I/O-every-task runtime plus global_queue_interval(1), compared against I/O-every-task alone. Three mixed repetitions per variant, only one private/room sample each. Rejected; source restored byte-identically to event-only archive and normal global-queue defaults.

datagram_scope: 32 self-route sessions, one outstanding echo each, eight seconds, 1 KiB, four server/four client workers. Direct fixed client verifies complete received bytes. Diagnostic only; not saturation/fanout/mixed datagram acceptance. CPU includes brief setup/teardown. No submitted-send count masquerades as received throughput.
profiles_scope: Separate cycles user+kernel captures attach both server and client at the ready gate. Reports filter by process PID and use relative percentages within that filtered process, self samples, no inclusive stacking. All four reports have zero lost samples. The syscall/stack capture is excluded from ordinary medians and does not measure all host softirq work.
kernel_scope: SOCK_DIAG counters at quiescent gates, independently inode-matched to each process and validated against real sockets/ss. Diagnostic scans are excluded from ordinary CPU/throughput medians. TCP/UDP socket-object size estimates come from read-only slab metadata, not process RSS. Buffer limits are not allocations and skmem counters are not all additive. These measurements exclude slab/allocator overhead, other networking state and active-traffic peaks. TIME_WAIT has no live fd: report port-matched counts separately, without attributing object bytes or claiming complete kernel memory. Both endpoints accounted separately; no complete total-system memory ratio is claimed.
freshness_scope: One regression sample per mode/profile, not statistical rankings. 360 states at 60 Hz over six seconds, 1 KiB each, plus 1 MiB reliable bulk. Loss: 20 ms one-way plus 2%; reorder also adds 8 ms jitter and 25% reorder, external port both directions in a disposable namespace. Matching seeds do not produce identical lost packets. Count unreceived updates explicitly; stale states cannot replace newer state.
remaining: Full throughput and memory parity remains unmet. Mixed private delivery still trails WS substantially, and the current runtime retains much larger per-connection userspace state. Full datagram saturation/private/fanout/mixed measurement, active kernel-buffer peaks/remaining accounting, observer cancellation/re-subscribe and concurrent 100k/8192 inspection, broader overload/shutdown, final packaging/deployment documentation and final acceptance remain outstanding. No release, push or deployment.
